name: The Blanchard household — a name the town's own records carry
head: blanchard_f_gantry

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. tax_1833 stands against this person's name by 31 December 1833 and nothing says when they came. THE 1833 TAX LIST IS A PROPERTY ROLL, NOT A RESIDENCE CHECK (T-1117): it names the owner of ground inside the town, resident or not, and its own entry 110 is a man three years dead. It bounds the town's RECORD of this name and not the day this person reached Chicago. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the town's own paper carries this name by 1 July 1835; whether the man it names was standing in the town is a claim this record cannot make, and present_on_scene_date says `uncertain` for that reason.

arrival_year.note: DRAWN, NOT READ. The household's arrival block holds a BOUND — somebody was here by 1833-12-31 and no source says when they came — so the year is drawn from the arrival years the known layer records, truncated at that bound and renormalised. It says what a household of this bound most likely was, and nothing whatever about this household.

basis.note: data/reconstruction/1835_town_model.json#arrival_and_origin.tables.arrival_year_of_the_known_layer, restricted to years at or before 1833.

replaceable_by.match: a dated source that says which year this household came to Chicago

origin.note: DRAWN FROM A SURVIVORSHIP SAMPLE. No source says where this household came from. The region is drawn from the birthplaces of the seventy Old Settlers who registered an arrival at or before 1835 — a self-selected roll set down forty-four years later that over-represents the men who stayed and prospered, as the town model's own open questions say. It is the only origin distribution this project holds and this value is drawn from it, not measured.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says where this household came from

reason_for_coming.value: The 1833 season: the harbour appropriation, the treaty at Chicago and the first rush of settlers
reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THE SEASON AND NOTHING ELSE. No trade is recorded for this household and no source says why it came; the only thing the evidence gives is when it was here by. This states the draws that were operating in that season and chooses among them nowhere. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

basis.note: arrival_fill.cohort_reasons — the household's arrival year (1833) is the only thing about it this value rests on.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says why this household came, or a committed source that apportions the town's arrivals between the land sales, the canal and the harbour works

lives_at.note: Not attested: the lists that name this person give no address. The placement sweep assigns homes once the resident list is complete (T-0514, the owner's own sequencing) and this pass will not guess one.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded here, so there is no premises to seek; T-0633 is where a later directory's address gets back-projected.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE RECORD BRACKETS THE DAY. This person is named at Chicago at or before 1 July 1835 and named again at or after it, so the sources reach across the scene date rather than stopping at one side of it. Inferred, not documented: no source says where they were on the day.

modelled_family.note: The kin core only. A servant, an apprentice or a journeyman this house may have held is priced by T-1183 and seated by T-1173; a boarder is seated by T-1175. The drawn size is a floor on the house.

persons.name: F Gantry Blanchard

later_occupation.note: NONE RECORDED FOR 1835 — AND A TRADE IS RECORDED FOR 1839. This is a POINTER at `directories.people[].occupation_later` on this same record, derived by `tools/qualify_later_trades.py` and holding nothing that block does not already say. It is not a claim about the scene date: the 1835 occupation above still reads `none_recorded`, its grade has not moved, and no premises has been sought on the strength of it, because a directory of 1839 is evidence about 1839. It is written because the field a reader consults was asserting an absence this file contradicts three lines further down, and "no trade anywhere" and "no trade in the scene window, one printed 1839" are not the same fact (T-0693).

occupation.note: No source in this pass's evidence records an occupation for this person. A poll list, a tax list, a muster roll and a baptismal entry each print a name and no trade, and where a later directory prints one it is a trade of 1843 — T-0633 is the rule for back-projecting that, and this pass does not have it.

dated_bounds.list_title: Illinois Public Domain Land Tract Sales Database — the federal land offices' sale registers, indexed by the Illinois State Archives
dated_bounds.locator: purchase 0367525, volume 817 page 027, section 16, T39N R14E
dated_bounds.identity_rule: NAMED, NOT UPHELD — the mechanical rule never proposed this one and could not. `namesake.choose` weighs the FIRST forename token, and the register prints this man's MIDDLE name in the forename's place, so GURTREY was put to all the Blanchards the town holds and named none of them. What names him is the town's own directory: Fergus 1843 prints 'Blanchard, Francis Gurtrey, capitalist, res 45 Wells [died, Brooklyn, N.Y., 1872.]' — forename Francis, middle name Gurtrey — and Fergus 1839 and Norris 1844 print the same man 'Francis G.' GURTREY is that middle name, and the card carries it as Gantry because the poll of 1834 prints him 'Blanchard, F. Gantry'. THE REGISTER PROVES ITS OWN HABIT HERE, AT ONE SALE. The six GURTREY rows (purchase nos 0367525-0367530, volume 817 page 027) and the three F G rows (0376893-0376895, volume 818 page 010) are the SAME school section — section 16, T39N R14E, type SC — entered on 22 and 24 October 1833, the days the school section was sold off by lot and by block. One buyer, one auction, two volumes of the register, two renderings of one name; the domain's README already records this habit under T-0990, where HUNTER E E and HUNTER EDWARD E are the same 80 acres of section 13 on the same day at the same price. WHAT IS NOT NAMED BY IT. The town's other documented Blanchard is W. G. Blanchard, the house-and-land agent of the Democrat of 9 July 1834, and his forename initial is W: he is refused on the same ground the crosswalk refuses him against every other Blanchard reading. Joseph Blanchard the blacksmith is a man of the directories and not an 1835 resident. Nothing reached prints a second Gurtrey Blanchard anywhere. AND IT IS STILL A PURCHASE. The Residence column reads UNKNOWN on all six rows, so this names a buyer and never an occupant, and it places nobody on that ground. The six rows are lot 1 of block 2, block 21, lot 8 of block 141, block 3, lot 7 of block 82 and lot 1 of block 141 of the school section, $547.00 in all (ls0076-ls0081). Two of them state a price per acre of 3.69 against 0000.00 acres, which is the acreage of the F G row ls0074 standing in the wrong column of the deposit; it is carried as the register has it and read as no acreage at all.
dated_bounds.note: A DATED APPEARANCE IN A LAND REGISTER, AND NOTHING FURTHER. The Residence column reads UNKNOWN, which places this purchaser nowhere: the register did not record where the purchaser lived. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. tax_1833 stands against this person's name by 31 December 1833 and nothing says when they came. THE 1833 TAX LIST IS A PROPERTY ROLL, NOT A RESIDENCE CHECK (T-1117): it names the owner of ground inside the town, resident or not, and its own entry 110 is a man three years dead. It bounds the town's RECORD of this name and not the day this person reached Chicago. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the town's own paper carries this name by 1 July 1835; whether the man it names was standing in the town is a claim this record cannot make, and present_on_scene_date says `uncertain` for that reason. No figure is drawn (L1). THE TOWN'S OWN ROLLS, 1833-1835 — CORROBORATION, NOT A GRADE. The early Chicago voter and tax lists held by the Illinois Regional Archives Depository name this person 1 time: Election returns — poll list of 1834, filed 11 August 1834 — “Blanchard, F. Gantry” (poll_1834_013, line 182). These are the town's own contemporary paper rather than a recollection of it, and each appearance says that a man of that name stood on that roll in that year — no more. The reading is twice mediated (Schulz's transcription, then Genealogy Trails' republication) and this project has not seen the IRAD originals. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) the 1835 poll with a second independent source is attested, the 1835 poll alone or a 1833/1834 list with another source is inferred, and a single appearance with nothing else is a projected resident. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE — T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: one resident of the surname 'Blanchard' agrees with the entry's forenames; 2 bearer(s) of the surname were considered. (data/research/civic/voter_crosswalk.json). FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “Fra’s G. Blanchard” (f1839_v0272, printed page 43, ward 2, voting for William B. Ogden). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'Blanchard' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins F. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 12 times, as “BLANCHARD F G”, “BLANCHARD F G AS”, “BLANCHARD GURTREY”, “BLANCHARD FRANCIS G”, 1833-10-22 to 1836-06-27: 1 federal land entry — NW sec 36 T38N R14E and 2 lots in the platted town — lot 2 of block 55 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L2BL55CHIOT, as printed); lot 7 of block 50 in the town the register codes CHIOTV (L7BL50CHIOTV, as printed) and 9 parcels of the school section — BL21 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL3 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; BL4 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), as read; lot 1 of block 141 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 1 of block 2 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 2 of block 26 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 7 of block 26 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 7 of block 82 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E); lot 8 of block 141 of the school section (sec 16 T39N R14E), 163.69 acres stated in all, for $5070.00 (ls0073, ls0074, ls0988, ls0989, ls0075, ls0076, ls0077, ls0078, ls0079, ls0080, ls0081, ls0715). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE SCHOOL-SECTION ROWS ARE GROUND INSIDE THE TOWN, NOT FARMLAND: section 16 of T39N R14E was platted and sold off by lot and by block at the sale of 1833, which is why the register states 0000.00 acres against most of them. Ground inside the town is nearer to this reconstruction than a quarter-section is, and it is still a purchase: the register names a purchaser and never an occupant, and nothing here puts this person on that ground. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $4150.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: BLANCHARD F G matches F Gantry Blanchard: the forename names F Gantry Blanchard of the 2 people of this surname, and the forename agrees as an initial only. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.

merge_ruling.for_merge: The surname, the middle initial G, and a trade that would suit either man: a house-and-land agent of 1834 and a real-estate dealer of 1839 are the same business. That is a coincidence of trade in a town where land was the trade, and it moves nothing against two different forename initials.
merge_ruling.against_merge: W. G. Blanchard is a house-and-land agent the Chicago Democrat names on 9 July 1834, and his forename initial is W. Francis Gurtrey Blanchard's is F. Two explicit and different forename initials on two documented men is D1, and the register's own crosswalk refuses W. G. against every Blanchard reading it holds on the same ground.

merge_ruling.for_merge: 'F. G.' agrees with 'F. Gantry' initial for initial, the surnames differ by one letter (c against s) in a ten-letter name, and 'Blanshard' is set NOWHERE in the deposited corpus — not once — while Blanchard is set 65 times. A stem with no independent life in the corpus is the shape a mis-set card usually takes.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE TOWN HOLDS TWO BLANSHARDS, AND NO TITLE SETS BOTH SPELLINGS. Against the corpus silence stands the resident layer: blanshard_f_g and blanshard_g are two cards of that spelling, so within this town the stem is populated in its own right and a fold of one of them says nothing about the other. The readings do not touch: 'Blanchard, F. Gantry' is the poll of 1834 and 'Blanchard, Gantry' the tax list of 1833, with Fergus 1843 ('Francis Gurtrey Blanchard, capitalist, res 45 Wells') and Norris 1844 ('Francis G.') behind them; 'F. G. Blanshard' is the Democrat of 12 November 1834 (#c012) and nothing else. No single printing is caught setting both spellings for one man. D7 — and the `blanchard` cluster's C8 merge of Gantry onto F. Gantry is untouched, because that fold had the directory printing the name whole and this one has nothing of the kind.
